q-64991.name: Question 1
q-64991.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-2\le x<0,\,0\le y<2}
$$

The interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,,\,0<y<2\,}.
$$

What is the missing expression?
q-64991.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14114523/assets/71851a12f638da9604450cae0d50ed15187e850368890845d60b16b89e728bcf.png)

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14114523/assets/abdd434da59bb3a1bdc0ee7de398d7ea4aeae2f617f54b5a26a5bad871ba0ac4.png)

So, in this case, the interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-2<x<0,\,0<y<2\,}.
$$

The boundary of a set A, denoted ∂A, is the set that contains all the boundary points of A.

The set A and its boundary ∂A are shown below.

The interior of a set A, denoted intA, is the set containing all the interior points of A. It contains every point in A except the boundary points: intA=A−∂A

q-161622.name: Question 2
q-161622.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,y\ge -1+x}.
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $A$ contains all of its boundary points.
- $A$ contains none of its boundary points.
- $\text{int}\,A=A$
q-161622.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

In this case, the set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14114523/assets/3e7d8c11ac4b3de8473741a362ad2b78555c764da2d61f955435e8d59771cf46.png)

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

Notice that, in this case, the set $A$ contains all of its boundary points. 

With that in mind, let's examine each statement:

- Statement I is true, while statement II is false. As we've seen, $A$ contains all of its boundary points.

- Statement III is false. Since $A$ contains all of its boundary points, we must have $A-∂A⊊A.$ Therefore $\text{int}\,A\ne A.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14114523/assets/69708aa698c38f8a29d3eb69083f893fd8fca183bd713387456624fc38b86fe9.png)

So, in this case, the interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}<4,\,0<x<2,\text{ }0<y<2}.
$$

Question 5
?

Consider the set A shown above. The interior of A is

intA={(x,y)∈R2:x2+y2<4,AAAA}.

What is the missing expression?

a
0<x<2, 0<y<2
b
0≤x≤2, 0≤y≤2
c
0≤x≤2, 0<y<2
d
0<x<2, 0≤y≤2
e
0≤x<2, 0≤y<2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The boundary of a set A, denoted ∂A, is the set that contains all the boundary points of A.

The set A and its boundary ∂A are shown below.

The interior of a set A, denoted intA, is the set containing all the interior points of A. It contains every point in A except the boundary points: intA=A−∂A

The interior of A is shown below.

So, in this case, the interior of A is given by

intA={(x,y)∈R2:x2+y2<4,0<x<2, 0<y<2}.
